top_story.headline: Education Department plans $352 million sole-source follow-on for Accenture's student-loan platforms
top_story.dek: The justification cites eight years of incumbent knowledge and about $23 million in switching costs.
paragraphs: Federal Student Aid plans to issue a logical follow-on task order to Accenture Federal Services LLC for the continued operation, maintenance and enhancement of its student, borrower and partner platforms, at an estimated $352,153,142 over up to 27 months, according to a justification posted on SAM.gov.

The document says Accenture has run the systems for more than eight years, holds undocumented knowledge of interfaces and legacy code, and that switching vendors would cost about $23 million in transition costs. The order goes through a National Institutes of Health government-wide contract.

Separately, the General Services Administration's White House Service Center posted two sole-source justifications for urgent repairs at a Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling building it describes as operating under top-secret protocols; the values are redacted.

sections.headline: Education Department plans a $352 million sole-source follow-on for Accenture; White House Service Center buys urgent repair work without competition
paragraphs: 48 new sole-source justifications and 524 new solicitations in the October 4-5 window; 0 notices already covered in earlier editions are not repeated. Dollar figures below come only from values stated in the justification documents.

blocks.title: Education Department gives Accenture a $352 million follow-on to run student-loan platforms, no competition
meta: logical follow-on order, skipped competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: Federal Student Aid plans a task order, through a National Institutes of Health government-wide contract, for continued operation and enhancement of the platforms millions of borrowers, applicants and schools use, running up to 27 months. The justification says Accenture has operated the systems for more than eight years, holds undocumented knowledge of interfaces and legacy code, and that switching would cost about $23 million in transition costs. The document's own wording marks it as an incumbent follow-on for the second-largest value in today's batch.

blocks.title: General Services Administration's White House Service Center picks sole-source contractors for urgent repairs at a Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling building tied to the White House complex
meta: BSA Contractors, LLC; M&M Welding & Fabricators, Inc.
urgent need, no time to compete
General Services Administration (White House Service Center)
blocks.text: Two justifications dated October 5 cover masonry restoration and power washing, and heating and cooling repairs, at Building 410 at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, which the documents describe as operating under top-secret security protocols. Both say the work must begin on an October date that "cannot be disclosed because of security concerns," and the masonry document says BSA Contractors previously did work at the White House complex, the Blair House and the President's Guest House. The masonry justification itself states the agency plans to market ideas early next fiscal year "to proactively avoid the excessive number of sole source acquisitions that have resulted from urgency."

blocks.title: Air Force extends sole-source U-2 forecasting dashboard with Credence Management Solutions after the prior order lapsed on September 29
meta: limited-source order (follow-on to a federal supply schedule order)
blocks.text: The follow-on covers development and maintenance of a cloud-based analytics dashboard for U-2 logistics and fleet readiness. The justification says the current order expired September 29, 2026 and that a transition would leave the program without its forecasting tool; it was signed September 14, two weeks earlier, and cites the incumbent's 12 months of proprietary knowledge and a $2.5 million-plus switching cost.

blocks.title: Defense Threat Reduction Agency bridges its nuclear stockpile database contract to General Dynamics Information Technology because the competitive follow-on isn't ready
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The six-month sole-source bridge, with options up to twelve months, supports the Defense Stockpile Management Systems that maintain the national nuclear weapons stockpile database. The agency says its competitively awarded five-year task order expired September 28, 2026 and that the planned competitive follow-on will not be finished in time.

blocks.title: Energy Department bridges secure-facility bug-sweeping work to Olgoonik Solutions during a recompete delay
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The bridge covers technical surveillance countermeasures, TEMPEST, communications security, protected distribution systems and wireless security support for the department's Office of Environment, Health, Safety and Security. The justification says the incumbent has the cleared personnel (TS/SCI with polygraphs) and certified technicians a switch would disrupt.

sections.headline: No new contract awards of $100,000 or more to report
paragraphs: No new-to-report USAspending awards of $2 million or more, and none between $100,000 and $2 million, turned up in this edition's window.

paragraphs: No new apportionment files were approved by the Office of Management and Budget during the past five days (September 30–October 5, 2026). No spend plan updates were detected during this period.
